pages.title: One company. Several ways to create value.
pages.lead: Intent Solutions connects applied AI engineering, reusable software, research, education, products and media around one purpose: making useful technology work reliably inside real operations.
pages.takeaway: The estate is the work, knowledge, tools and relationships that reinforce the company. Its websites are entry points into that system.

diagram.description: Six company functions surround a shared Intent Solutions practice. The mission guides the practice. An emerging international engineering and commercial network would coordinate opportunities and delivery. A shared operating spine supports every function.

nodes.title: Client engineering
nodes.body: Frame an outcome; engineer workflows, integrations, agents and human controls.

nodes.title: Open source & tooling
nodes.body: Publish inspectable skills, plugins and developer tools.

nodes.title: Education & community
nodes.body: Practice engineering judgment through shared methods, artifacts and review.

nodes.title: Close the deployment gap
nodes.body: Turn changing AI capability into reliable, measurable work people can own and improve.

nodes.title: Intent Solutions
nodes.body: Frame → Build → Prove → Operate. Models and providers remain replaceable components.

nodes.title: Engineering network
nodes.body: Connect customers, originators and independent specialists through accountable coordination.

items.label: Terms and capacity still being established

nodes.title: Owned products
nodes.body: DiagnosticPro, Scorecard Echo and HustleStats apply the engineering to specific markets.

nodes.title: Research & evidence
nodes.body: Test behavior, preserve results and show working systems.

nodes.title: Content & media
nodes.body: Publish field notes, demos and explanations of permitted work.

notes.text: Shared operating spine: source and decisions · durable work tracking · governed knowledge · release evidence · production operations.

panels.title: A company architecture, with room to evolve
panels.body: These are functions that reinforce one another. A product or team may contribute to several functions; the map is not a fixed department chart.
items: The mission stays consistent while technologies and delivery methods change.
Public artifacts demonstrate capability at their own scope and maturity.
The emerging network is a model under development.

panels.title: One piece of work can serve several purposes
panels.body: A troubleshooting workflow can become a client implementation, an evaluated skill, a permitted demonstration and a lesson. Each use has its own permission, quality and maintenance requirements.
items: Private customer work stays private unless publication is authorized.
Portfolio discovery links to products with differing maturity.
Public adoption, community participation and contracted delivery are separate signals.

panels.title: Products make the breadth concrete
panels.body: Vertical products carry the engineering into repair diagnostics, live baseball analysis and youth soccer development. Other products package the underlying engineering methods themselves.
items: DiagnosticPro: repair diagnostics and work planning.
Scorecard Echo: a baseball broadcast-booth companion.
HustleStats: youth soccer performance tracking.
Bob’s Big Brain and the Intent Eval Platform: governed knowledge and evaluation infrastructure.
Intent Longbox: collectibles intake-to-commerce, in development.

panels.title: The external ecosystem has a place
panels.body: Learn links public Anthropic-issued credential evidence. Claude, OpenAI, Gemini and local models remain technology choices to assess against the work; the shared engineering standard extends across vendor ecosystems.
items: Credential evidence has a defined scope; it does not establish the whole company’s delivery capacity.
Vendor learning and open-source contributions can strengthen capability and relationships.
Tons of Skills is model-neutral at its canonical source layer; Claude Code is its currently verified-native harness.

sources.label: Network direction and six-function framing: owner-supplied vision, October 2026.

pages.title: How one piece of work can compound.
pages.kicker: Macro to micro / the intended business loop
pages.lead: Engineering creates more than a finished implementation. With clear permissions, evidence and ownership, it can also create reusable assets, teaching material and new questions worth solving.
pages.takeaway: Compounding requires deliberate choices at each handoff. Attention, adoption, qualified demand and revenue are different outcomes.

diagram.description: A real workflow problem moves through engineering and evidence to a rights and reuse decision. Work may remain private or become tools, knowledge or products. Use and audience feedback can create qualified conversations and better briefs that restart the loop. This is an intended operating model, not a proven revenue engine.

nodes.title: Real workflow
nodes.body: A problem, its constraints, an intended outcome and a way to judge success.

nodes.title: Engineering
nodes.body: Integrate, build, handle exceptions and establish operating ownership.

nodes.title: Evidence
nodes.body: Test the behavior, record limits and use failures to change the work.

nodes.title: Rights & reuse
nodes.body: Choose what stays private and what can be released, taught or productized.

nodes.title: Retained capability
nodes.body: Client-specific knowledge, protected IP and operating documentation.

nodes.title: Reusable tools
nodes.body: Skills, plugins, integrations and source others can inspect and adapt.

nodes.title: Shared knowledge
nodes.body: Demos, lessons, field notes and research with their evidence and limits.

nodes.title: Focused products
nodes.body: A maintained product when a repeated need supports a distinct offering.

nodes.title: A sharper brief
nodes.body: Reuse lessons and test the next problem.

nodes.title: Qualified relationship
nodes.body: Establish fit, authority and a real need.

nodes.title: Discovery & trust
nodes.body: People inspect, learn, adopt and ask.

nodes.title: Use & operations
nodes.body: Observe friction, failures and new needs.

notes.text: A failed test sends the work back for correction before it can support a wider claim.

panels.title: The gates give the loop meaning
panels.body: Useful output does not automatically become public IP or a product. Rights, audience need, evidence and an ongoing owner determine which path is appropriate.
items: A demo needs permission and a truthful account of what it demonstrates.
An open-source component needs a license and a maintenance boundary.
A product needs a defined user problem and an operating plan.

panels.title: Feedback has several jobs
panels.body: Failure can revise architecture; product use can expose another need; teaching can reveal a missing explanation. Commercial qualification tests whether an interested audience has a problem the company should take on.
items: Adoption can demonstrate interest without proving willingness to pay.
Credentials and community activity can demonstrate learning without proving capacity.
The intended loop still needs evidence of repeatable commercial conversion.

panels.title: An illustrative walkthrough
panels.body: A repeated support task could produce an integration, a test case, a reusable troubleshooting skill and a lesson. That is a design example of how assets connect, not a reported client outcome.
items: The deployed task retains its own owner and acceptance criteria.
Only permitted, reusable parts enter public distribution.
Later use informs the next version of the tool and the next brief.

sources.label: Routing and commercial feedback: owner-directed intended operating model.

pages.title: From an outcome to an owned operation
pages.lead: Frame → Build → Prove → Operate is the shared method. Each handoff carries a concrete artifact, an acceptance condition, and a responsible person.
pages.takeaway: The customer receives a working capability and the means to evolve it. A deployment is incomplete while operating ownership is unresolved.

diagram.description: Four delivery stages connect left to right. Each produces an artifact below. A failed release decision sends work back to the build; operational findings return to the scope and baseline. This is the delivery method, not a record of universal implementation.

regions.label: SHARED METHOD · APPLY TO THE ACTUAL ENGAGEMENT
HANDOFF ARTIFACTS · DEFINE OWNER AND ACCEPTANCE

nodes.title: Agree what must change
nodes.body: Observe the workflow with the people who own it. Define the useful result, constraints, baseline, and human decisions.

nodes.title: Engineer the whole workflow
nodes.body: Connect data, systems, models, and tools. Build exception paths and controls alongside the useful behavior.

nodes.title: Test the claim in context
nodes.body: Evaluate representative work and failure cases. Review the result against the agreed standard, including its limits.

items.label: A demo is one piece of evidence

nodes.title: Transfer, run, and improve
nodes.body: Establish monitoring, rollback, response, and ownership. Transfer the access and knowledge the customer needs.

items.label: A capable customer is an outcome

nodes.title: Outcome brief
nodes.body: Scope, baseline, success test, decision rights, data boundaries, and the intended handoff.

nodes.title: Versioned candidate
nodes.body: Source, configuration, integration contracts, operating assumptions, and testable behavior.

nodes.title: Evidence + release decision
nodes.body: Results, failures, acceptance, and authorization to release. Unmet conditions return to engineering.

nodes.title: Operating handoff
nodes.body: Runbook, access, owner, rollback, incident path, knowledge transfer, and review cadence.

edges.label: Operating evidence → changed baseline, scope, or next problem

panels.title: Acceptance is a shared decision
panels.body: The customer owns the business acceptance criteria and the authority it retains. The agreed engagement identifies who may approve scope, release, and changes.
items: The delivery lead assembles evidence and resolves failed conditions.
The operating owner accepts the runbook and failure response.
A tool-generated pass never replaces required human authorization.

panels.title: Independence is designed into the handoff
panels.body: Documentation, access, training, maintenance responsibilities, and an exit path belong in the delivery plan from the beginning.
items: Use customer constraints to decide where systems run.
Agree support responsibilities and escalation before release.
Revisit provider and architecture choices when evidence changes.

sources.label: Owner-directed operating model; handoff artifacts are a method specification, not a completed-engagement claim.

pages.title: The operating spine underneath the estate.
pages.kicker: Micro / durable context, coordinated work and operations
pages.lead: People and agents need to know what is authoritative, what work is ready, what has been learned and what is safe to release. Separate systems hold those responsibilities; shared interfaces make them usable together.
pages.takeaway: The model can change without losing the company’s source, work history or governed knowledge. Durable state belongs to systems with explicit owners and rules.

diagram.description: Three durable authorities hold source and decisions, Beads work state and governed knowledge. Skills, MCP tools and agent sessions use those authorities to perform bounded work. Review and release gates connect work to deployment, operation and new evidence. Arrows show responsibility and information flow, not a claim that every integration is fully automated.

regions.label: DURABLE AUTHORITIES / EACH HAS A DISTINCT JOB

nodes.title: Source & decisions
nodes.body: Source code, company policies, interface contracts, operating docs and recorded decisions.

nodes.title: Durable work
nodes.body: Issues, dependencies, claims, acceptance evidence and task history across sessions.

items.label: Dolt database authority · Git code history

nodes.title: Governed knowledge
nodes.body: Capture proposals, apply governance, retrieve cited knowledge and verify audit receipts.

nodes.title: Skills
nodes.body: Specify the method, required context and completion conditions for a class of work.

nodes.title: MCP & tool interfaces
nodes.body: Expose bounded tools and retrieval. Access still follows the tool’s permissions.

nodes.title: People & agent sessions
nodes.body: Recover context, claim work, act within scope and leave evidence for the next session.

nodes.title: Review & release gates
nodes.body: Check acceptance, tests, changes and required human decisions before release.

nodes.title: Deployment
nodes.body: Versioned release, verification and an available rollback path.

nodes.title: Operation
nodes.body: Observe health, respond to failures and maintain recovery procedures.

nodes.title: Evidence & proposals
nodes.body: Record what changed. Propose useful lessons for governed recall.

panels.title: Each authority answers a different question
panels.body: Source records what exists and what was decided. Work tracking records what remains and why it is blocked. Governed memory records what may be recalled as an accepted lesson.
items: An index is a rebuildable search aid, not a replacement authority.
A dashboard is a projection with a scope and freshness boundary.
A proposed memory is not accepted knowledge merely because an agent wrote it.

panels.title: Bob’s Big Brain, closer in
panels.body: The Compiler can derive knowledge from a source corpus. The Registrar applies governance and maintains receipts; qmd supplies cited retrieval. The plugin exposes that loop through tools and skills.
items: Local mode operates in process after provisioning.
Team mode proxies to a shared governed-brain service.
The Compiler itself is a local tool; a team interface does not prove every ingestion path is deployed.

panels.title: Coordination without pretending everything is automatic
panels.body: The estate combines source, tools and operating procedures at different stages of adoption. People remain responsible for scope, promotion, release, response and recovery.
items: Beads history and code history travel in different Git reference lanes.
Hooks restore context and apply local guardrails; review and CI enforce their release checks.
Capabilities and rollout status must be checked in their owning repository.
Operational proof includes failure and recovery behavior, not just a passing build.

panels.title: The business and operations support layer
panels.body: The spine also connects relationship management, project coordination, communication and operational awareness. Each tool retains a defined job; a shared view does not make every system one synchronized authority.
items: Twenty supports relationship tracking; Plane provides a project-coordination surface alongside Beads work records.
Mission Control projects scoped status from the owning systems, preserving source, freshness and unknown states.
MXroute handles company email; Buzz supports team conversations and notification surfaces.
Monitoring, alert routing, backups and restore procedures support the person accountable for operations.
The public Mission Control view is a bounded reporting projection, not the private operations console.

sources.label: Governed brain plugin and team mode

pages.title: From a claim to a release decision.
pages.kicker: Micro / research, contracts, evaluation and proof
pages.lead: A useful evaluation names the task, criteria, scope and result. The Intent Eval Platform separates methodology, executable checks, shared evidence contracts and rollout decisions so the conclusion can be inspected.
pages.takeaway: Labs investigates and explains. Evals defines result meanings. Harnesses perform checks. A rollout policy decides whether a specific result permits a release.

diagram.description: The six-repository Intent Eval Platform connects Lab methodology and Core contracts to task cases, deterministic checks and behavioral evaluation. Checks emit an Evidence Bundle; the rollout gate combines it with a policy and emits a decision record for the dashboard. Failure returns to the test or implementation. This shows the architecture, not universal deployment coverage.

regions.label: APPLY POLICY AND RECORD THE DECISION

nodes.title: Intent Eval Lab
nodes.body: Define the question, test method, failure cases and interpretation limits.

nodes.title: Intent Eval Core
nodes.body: Versioned types, schemas, validators and state definitions make results comparable.

nodes.title: Task cases & criteria
nodes.body: Choose representative work, expected behavior and cases that must fail.

nodes.title: Audit Harness
nodes.body: Check declared source and test-policy requirements with reproducible gates.

nodes.title: J-Rig
nodes.body: Exercise an artifact against explicit criteria; preserve observations and judgments.

nodes.title: Evidence Bundle
nodes.body: Carry the result, scope and supporting evidence in the platform’s versioned contract.

nodes.title: Rollout policy
nodes.body: State which results permit this release and which conditions must block it.

nodes.title: Intent Rollout Gate
nodes.body: Apply a policy to the supplied evidence and record the decision.

nodes.title: Signed decision record
nodes.body: Preserve the decision and its evidence reference for later inspection.

nodes.title: Intent Eval Dashboard
nodes.body: Expose methodology and available results with their scope and freshness.

notes.text: Published results are scoped observations, not blanket certification.

panels.title: Six repositories, one evidence language
panels.body: Lab, Core, Audit Harness, J-Rig, Rollout Gate and Dashboard retain separate responsibilities and releases. Their shared contracts connect the work without pretending they are one monolithic service.
items: Methodology and contracts define what the result means.
Executable checks generate observations for the declared task.
A rollout rule turns evidence into a bounded release decision.

panels.title: A failure is useful information
panels.body: A failed evaluation can block a release and identify what must change. A missing or stale result establishes uncertainty; it must not silently become a pass or an invented failure.
items: The task, version and test conditions belong with the result.
A passing example does not establish performance for every workflow.
The same discipline applies when the model or provider changes.

panels.title: What can be inspected today
panels.body: The public Lab includes scoped skill evaluation examples and methodology. Its published boundary is explicit: skill checks run locally; agent loops and workflows need a custom test setup.
items: Demos show behavior and link evidence where available.
Evals preserves definitions for interpreting records.
The diagram explains the architecture; current integration coverage belongs to the source repositories.

pages.title: People, practice and permission to deliver
pages.lead: People can learn, contribute, introduce opportunities or deliver specialist work. Each responsibility needs its own evidence and authority.
pages.takeaway: Joining the practice, earning a credential, demonstrating capability and accepting a customer engagement are different decisions.

diagram.description: Current practice entry requires human review and verified agreements. The reviewer may request clarification, pause or decline. Proposed customer-work qualification checks role evidence and current fit separately; insufficient evidence returns for reassessment, while unavailable capacity pauses assignment. Practice access never grants customer-delivery authority.

regions.label: 02 / CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITY · PROPOSED QUALIFICATION AND AUTHORIZATION

nodes.title: Request access
nodes.body: Share relevant work, your contribution and why the practice fits.

nodes.title: Human review
nodes.body: Resolve material gaps and decide whether to continue the introduction.

nodes.title: Onboarding agreements
nodes.body: Complete the applicable NDA and User Agreement before access release.

nodes.title: Join the practice
nodes.body: Receive the welcome, resources and approved account access.

nodes.title: Clarify, pause or decline
nodes.body: A request can stop here. New evidence can be reviewed.

nodes.title: Engineering evidence
nodes.body: Explain the implementation, tradeoffs and failure handling.

nodes.title: Commercial evidence
nodes.body: Show discovery, opportunity quality or domain judgment.

nodes.title: Assess capability
nodes.body: Compare the work with the role and responsibility.

nodes.title: Confirm engagement fit
nodes.body: Check capacity, scope, conflicts and willingness to accept this work.

nodes.title: Authorize specific work
nodes.body: Agree deliverables, acceptance and the accountable lead.

nodes.title: Develop and reassess
nodes.body: Return with useful evidence. No capability is assumed.

nodes.title: No current fit
nodes.body: No assignment. Reconsider when circumstances change.

notes.text: A human decision determines progression. A persuasive application does not bypass review.
Practice access supports learning and relationships. It does not promise work or authorize representation of Intent Solutions.
Delivery evidence informs future assessments. Recheck capacity for every engagement.

panels.title: Many ways to contribute
panels.body: Engineers, architects, commercial originators, domain experts and independent firms can contribute different kinds of value. A code-only admission test would miss much of that value.
items: Assess the contribution relevant to the role.
Allow private-work descriptions when public artifacts are unavailable.
Treat credentials as optional evidence within a wider record.

panels.title: What is real today
panels.body: Practice intake, human review and agreement-based onboarding exist. That operating capability is distinct from a fully calibrated international delivery network.
items: Current onboarding does not measure the entire community’s delivery capacity.
A membership count is not an available engineering roster.
Further assessment, commercial readiness and project authorization remain separate.

panels.title: What the stronger gate must establish
panels.body: Before assigning customer responsibility, the proposed model needs evidence for the work, the capacity and the agreement. The acceptance standard follows the responsibility.
items: Comparable work reviewed against role-specific criteria.
A current commitment for a bounded engagement.
An accountable lead, signed scope and a defined escalation path.

sources.label: Owner-provided operating brief; current onboarding records reviewed for this atlas

pages.title: The emerging international network
pages.lead: The proposed seventh arm connects customers, commercial originators, independent specialists and firms around work with clear responsibility.
pages.takeaway: Intent must earn its role through identifiable value. Each engagement defines who contributes, who contracts and who answers for the outcome.

diagram.description: Customers, originators and delivery specialists interact through an Intent coordinating layer inside one engagement boundary. Below them are three families of possible arrangements. The model is proposed, participants may hold multiple roles, and independent business remains outside the boundary.

regions.label: ONE ENGAGEMENT · SELECTED ROLES, EXPLICIT AUTHORITY, DEFINED RESPONSIBILITY
ARRANGEMENT FOLLOWS CONTRIBUTION · COMMERCIAL MODELS TO VALIDATE

nodes.title: Customers
nodes.body: Bring the operating context and the authority to define and accept the work.

nodes.title: Origination
nodes.body: Develop qualified opportunities and clarify why the work matters.

nodes.title: Intent operating layer
nodes.body: Assemble the engagement and make responsibilities inspectable.

nodes.title: Execution
nodes.body: Bring capable people, relevant assets and an agreed delivery commitment.

items.label: Scope and capacity confirmed for the work

nodes.title: Referral or presales
nodes.body: Define the opportunity, attribution and responsibility.

nodes.title: Subcontract or joint delivery
nodes.body: Define parties, scope, acceptance and risk allocation.

nodes.title: Managed work and support
nodes.body: Define ownership, service boundaries and the exit path.

notes.text: Participants may hold multiple roles. Joining the network does not assign unrelated customers, business or intellectual property to Intent.

panels.title: What Intent has to contribute
panels.body: The coordinating layer has to provide something the engagement needs. Its role can combine opportunity development, architecture, reusable engineering, contractual accountability, quality control and operations.
items: Identify the contribution before setting the arrangement.
Name the customer-facing accountable party for that engagement.
Avoid a universal claim that Intent owns every independent relationship.

panels.title: International by design, explicit in execution
panels.body: Independent people and firms can operate across countries, but a shared vision does not settle the legal form of their relationship. Geography, entity type and the actual work shape the appropriate arrangement.
items: Confirm jurisdiction, entity status and authorized signers.
Resolve IP, confidentiality, security and liability for the scope.
Use legal review to support the chosen commercial model.

panels.title: What still needs validation
panels.body: The network is a business model being developed. Repeatable customer acquisition, committed capacity, workable incentives and sustainable delivery economics must be established through actual engagements.
items: Choose a narrow initial offer and customer segment.
Prove one complete engagement and its operating responsibility.
Measure margin after delivery, coordination, support and risk costs.
Expand only from evidence about demand, delivery and contribution.

tables.title: Commercial hypotheses to test
tables.description: These are possible arrangements, not published offers or agreed terms. A signed engagement must identify the payer, deliverer, responsibility, costs and acceptance conditions.
rows: A usable scope and an accountable handoff

Demand, service boundaries and delivery cost
Independent learning value and practical feedback
Learning outcomes, delivery cost and permitted offer
A maintained solution to a repeated problem
Retention, operating cost and willingness to pay

pages.title: A consistent mission. Evolving methods.
pages.kicker: Governing principles and the next decisions
pages.lead: The estate needs enough consistency for people to work together and enough freedom to adapt as models, markets and operating conditions change.
pages.takeaway: Keep the outcome, evidence and accountability clear. Adapt the technology, delivery structure and commercial experiments as the work teaches us.

diagram.description: Six operating principles connect to one central mission. Model independence, evidence and reusable intellectual property sit on the left. Opportunity without entitlement, distributed accountability and adaptation sit on the right. The central standard survives changes in models, tools and organization.

nodes.title: Model agnostic by design
nodes.body: Choose models and vendors for the work. One vendor relationship does not define the company.

nodes.title: Build, test, prove, operate
nodes.body: Pair implementation with evaluations, human controls and operating responsibility.

nodes.title: Compound useful IP
nodes.body: Turn relevant learning into reusable assets while respecting customer and contributor rights.

items.label: Owned assets · licensed reuse · open source

nodes.title: Reliable work in real businesses
nodes.body: Close the gap between AI capability and work an organization can trust, own and improve.

nodes.title: Opportunity is earned
nodes.body: Community, education, qualification and commercial authority are separate.

items.label: No automatic entitlement to paid work

nodes.title: Distribute capability
nodes.body: Work can span people, firms and countries while each engagement has clear responsibility.

items.label: Who decides · who delivers · who responds

nodes.title: Stay fluid with direction
nodes.body: Change tools, delivery methods and experiments when evidence supports the change.

notes.text: These principles explain the operating vision. Specific policies and contractual commitments require their own decisions and evidence.

panels.title: Established capabilities
panels.body: Public software, a skills marketplace, technical publishing, learning surfaces and working internal systems give the estate material to build on. Each artifact establishes a bounded capability.
items: Inspect the linked work and its current status.
Distinguish adoption and technical proof from customer conversion.
Keep public examples and their limitations understandable.

panels.title: Under development
panels.body: The next layer connects those capabilities to clearer commercial and delivery arrangements. Qualification, capacity, agreements and operating responsibility must fit together.
items: Role-specific qualification and current capacity.
Commercial arrangements and legal foundations.
A repeatable method for scoped, accountable engagements.

panels.title: Decisions that move the vision forward
panels.body: The first proof is a complete, useful engagement with a clear customer and an accountable delivery arrangement. Its lessons should improve the next one.
items: Choose the first offer, customer segment and acceptance test.
Name who can commit scope and who owns delivery and operations.
Define partner contribution, risks, margin measurement and exit.
Decide what learning is free, what may become paid, and why.
Record a decision owner and date for each unresolved choice.
